findings.reason: §8 already names the one addition and states in-text why the family cannot shrink, which satisfies the accounting rule as written; the private name is a cheaper variant of a compliant section, not a defect in the plan's own reasoning.
findings.text: §8 promotes `_write_through_sibling_temporary` to the public name `write_atomically` (+1 on public_definitions 1474), but all ~15 migrating call sites named in §8/§9 are in-package, so a private `_write_atomically` would hide the same behaviour behind the same interface and add no public surface; the section accounts for the addition ("the one addition is the price of a single owner") without stating why a private name is unavailable

interface_budget-1.reason: reckon/_store.py is a private module by its own name, so every definition in it is package-internal whatever its spelling; its sibling write_json_atomically follows the same convention, and a leading-underscore name imported across fifteen modules is the cross-module private use the naming rules discourage; the +1 is accounted for in the section

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 promotes one private primitive to a single public writer that hides temporary creation, `O_EXCL` retry, chmod, fsync, replace and cleanup; §9 adds one detection function over `definitions` and forbids new helper functions in every migrating module, so complexity sits behind small interfaces rather than behind a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names the owner to extend (`reckon/_store.py:write_atomically`) and routes the surviving forks to it; the census predicate is kept only as a frozen measurement, reconciled with the runtime rule by a parity assertion, which is a one-owner direction rather than a fork.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 adds `write_atomically` to the public-definitions family although every caller is inside the reckon package and a leading-underscore name serves them at zero public cost, and the section names the addition's cost without naming the private alternative.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the mechanism it extends for each section: `reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary` (§8), `reckon/interface_counts.py:read_trees`/`definitions` (§9), and the frozen census predicate `primitive_concepts` in `docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py`; all three exist and match the plan's description.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 explicitly justifies keeping `write_json_atomically` as the JSON adapter over the promoted name ("not a second owner of the mechanism") rather than as a parallel path, and §9 states "No new function is added to any migrating module".
